existing.description: The Petroleum Technology Development Fund, a Nigerian federal government agency, sponsors fully funded MSc and PhD places at its partner universities in the United Kingdom, Germany, France and Malaysia for Nigerian candidates in oil and gas related disciplines. The published benefits for the 2026 award are return flight tickets, health insurance, tuition and bench fees where applicable, and allowances for accommodation and living expenses. Application is made through the PTDF Scholarship Management Portal. The 2026 call closed on 27 February 2026 and the Fund has not yet published the 2027 call.
eligibility: Nigerian citizen with a Certificate of Indigeneship / Local Government Identification Letter
MSc: minimum Second Class Upper (2:1) first degree, or Second Class Lower (2:2) with relevant industry experience
PhD: at least Second Class Lower (2:2) first degree plus a good postgraduate degree
Mandatory National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) completed
Five (5) O-Level credits including English Language and Mathematics
Verified National Identity Number (NIN) before application; NIMC verification charges apply
Programme of study consistent with the applicant's prior academic background and relevant to the oil and gas industry
existing.eligibility_summary: Nigerian citizens who hold at least a Second Class Upper (2:1) first degree (or 2:2 with relevant industry experience for MSc), have completed the mandatory National Youth Service Corps, hold five O-Level credits including English Language and Mathematics, are computer literate, and have a verified National Identity Number.
benefits: Tuition and bench fees where applicable
Allowances for accommodation and living expenses
coverage: Allowances for accommodation and living expenses
requirements: Only PTDF-approved courses at PTDF partner institutions are eligible

UK PhD awards for the 2026 academic year are limited to split-site programmes at the College of Petroleum and Energy Studies, Kaduna (CPESK) with Robert Gordon University, University of Strathclyde or University of Portsmouth
PhD applicants intending to apply under the PTDF/DAAD partnership in Germany must secure a research supervisor before final selection interviews
Lecturers applying must submit a letter from their Vice-Chancellor confirming they are not benefiting from any other scholarship
MSc: Statement of Purpose of maximum 500 words
PhD: research proposal of maximum five pages covering topic, background, objectives, methodology and data collection approach
documents: First Degree Certificate or Statement of Result
WAEC/GCE/SSCE/NECO results and relevant PINs for online verification
Evidence of membership of relevant professional associations
application_method: Create an applicant account on the PTDF Scholarship Management Portal at scholarship.ptdf.gov.ng
Complete and submit the online application form with all documents scanned in PDF format
Shortlisted applicants are invited to a selection interview and must present transcripts in advance
existing.selection_notes: Initial screening is based on submitted qualifications, after which the top applicants in each category from each State are invited to interview. A selection committee assesses academic merit (quality of degrees, complete academic transcripts, relevant professional qualifications), relevant publications for PhD applicants, membership of professional bodies, and the viability and relevance of the study plan or research proposal. Multiple applications result in automatic disqualification, as does submission of illegible or falsified documents.
existing.best_fit: Nigerian graduates with a strong oil and gas academic record who have completed NYSC and are seeking a funded MSc or PhD at a PTDF partner university in the UK, Germany, France or Malaysia.
existing.application_period: 2026 cycle: call published 18 January 2026, applications closed 27 February 2026
existing.deadline_display: Six weeks from the date of publication of the call (2026 call closed 27 February 2026)
